He chairs the Public Investment Fund, whose sovereign holdings are state assets rather than evidence of his personal fortune.

long_biography.plain_text:
Prince Mohammed bin Salman was born in Riyadh and earned a law degree from King Saud University. He began public service at the Bureau of Experts to the Council of Ministers, later advising his father when Salman was governor of Riyadh and then crown prince. After King Salman took the throne, Mohammed became defence minister; he was named crown prince in 2017 and prime minister in 2022.

His public economic role centres on chairing the Council of Economic and Development Affairs and the Public Investment Fund, which is central to Saudi Vision 2030. PIF's own reporting defines it as a sovereign fund and public legal entity, so its portfolio is not evidence of his personal wealth. Independent reporting has attributed significant personal assets to structures linked to his foundation, but the underlying private wealth remains opaque and cannot be assigned confidently to an operating industry.
